title: High-Rate CO2 Electroreduction to C2+ Products over a Copper- Copper Iodide Catalyst
abstract: Electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) to multicarbon hydrocarbon and oxygenate (C2+) products with high energy density and wide availability is of great importance, as it provides a promising way to achieve the renewable energy storage and close the carbon cycle. Herein we design a Cu-CuI composite catalyst with abundant Cu/Cu + interfaces by physically mixing Cu nanoparticles and CuI powders. The composite catalyst achieves a remarkable C2+ partial current density of 591 mA cm −2 at −1.0 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode in a flow cell, substantially higher than Cu (329 mA cm −2 ) and CuI (96 mA cm −2 ) counterparts. Induced by alkaline electrolyte and applied potential, the Cu-CuI composite catalyst undergoes significant reconstruction under CO2RR conditions. Structural characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that the high-rate C2+ production over Cu-CuI is ascribed to the presence of residual Cu + and adsorbed iodine species which improve CO adsorption and facilitate C-C coupling. The overuse of fossil energy causes an imbalance in the carbon cycle, resulting in serious climate change. Electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) can convert CO2 into valuable fuels and chemicals utilizing renewable energy resources and surplus nuclear power, which can simultaneously achieve the electric energy storage and close the carbon cycle. However, the molecular structure of CO2 is very stable and many intermediates and products are involved in CO2RR, so that reaction pathways are complex and product selectivity is usually low. One of core aspects improving CO2RR performance is to develop catalysts with high activity, selectivity and stability. Electrochemically reducing CO2 to valuable hydrocarbons and oxygenates is of great interest, as they have high energy density and wide availability. Cu is the most active metal which converts CO2 into multi-carbon (C2+) products with considerable amounts. However, the generation of C2+ products with high selectivity and industrially-relevant production rate is still challenging. Currently, the reactivity of Cu catalysts is tuned via controlling size, morphology, composition, oxidation state and surface reconstruction. 4b-d, 5] Operando spectroscopy characterizations reveal that the presence of Cu species under CO2RR conditions correlates closely with the generation of C2+ products such as ethylene and ethanol. Theoretical studies propose that Cu/Cu interface in partially oxidized Cu matrix is favorable for CO2 activation and subsequent C-C coupling . Yet, Cu species tend to be readily reduced owing to the thermodynamic instability of Cu2O under CO2RR conditions. The depletion of Cu species is later retarded by doping Cu catalysts with secondary metals and heteroatoms such as sulfur, boron and halides that are considered to promote C-C coupling by stabilizing adjacent Cu species. 6a, 8] Moreover, halides either adsorbed on catalyst surface or present in electrolytes are argued to play a vital role in tuning the activity and selectivity of Cu catalysts. 9] Herein we design a Cu-CuI composite catalyst with abundant Cu/Cu interfaces by physically mixing Cu nanoparticles and CuI powders. The Cu-CuI composite catalyst achieves a remarkable C2+ partial current density of 591 mA cm at −1.0 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in a flow cell, much higher than Cu (329 mA cm) and CuI (96 mA cm) counterparts. Induced by alkaline electrolyte and applied potential, the Cu-CuI composite catalyst undergoes significant reconstruction under reaction conditions. The high-rate C2+ production over Cu-CuI is ascribed to the presence of residual Cu and adsorbed iodine species which improve CO adsorption and facilitate C-C coupling during CO2RR, as confirmed by structural characterizations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations.
